exercise.title: One badge counter
exercise.prompt:
The page holds a list `#tags` with several `button` children and a counter `#count` that starts at 0.

Attach exactly one click listener to `#tags` so that clicking any button, including buttons added to the list later, raises the number inside `#count` by one. Do not attach a listener to each button.

Example: three clicks on any mix of buttons leaves `#count` showing `3`.

tests.input: document.querySelectorAll('#tags button')[0].click(); return document.querySelector('#count').textContent === '1' ? 'ok' : 'count did not move';
tests.name: one click

tests.input: const b = document.querySelectorAll('#tags button'); b[0].click(); b[1].click(); return document.querySelector('#count').textContent === '2' ? 'ok' : 'two clicks failed';
tests.name: two clicks

tests.input: const nb = document.createElement('button'); document.querySelector('#tags').appendChild(nb); nb.click(); return document.querySelector('#count').textContent === '1' ? 'ok' : 'new button ignored';
return document.querySelector('#count').textContent === '0' ? 'ok' : 'counter did not start at zero';

exercise.referenceSolution:
<script>
  const list = document.querySelector('#tags');
  const out = document.querySelector('#count');
  list.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    if (e.target.tagName === 'BUTTON') out.textContent = String(Number(out.textContent) + 1);
  });
</script>
